mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (proxied by INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as production slowdowns impact corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO declines by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (proxied by PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real GDP (GDPC1) over the previous quarter signals a strengthening demand side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth accelerates.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and GDPC1 increase over the previous quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals deflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are squeezed by falling prices.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL decreases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a significant labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises & PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises and PAYEMS decreases by more than 100,000 in a month.
